findings.quote: practical counsel delivered for BOTH: correct the curator honoring her repentance AND require the catalog fixed; confront the assistant's settled pattern including stopping it, retracting the false claims to misled buyers, and proportionate discipline
findings.detail: One 1.0 all-or-nothing line bundles two full scenarios (a and b), each with 2-3 sub-requirements (5+ judgments). A grader cannot credit a model that nails (a)-counsel but omits (b)-counsel; per §5 the skeleton is '(1.0) practical counsel delivered per scenario' and §4.1 forbids multi-judgment lines.
findings.proposed_fix: Split into two 0.5 lines: (0.5) '(a) counsel: correct the curator honoring her repentance AND require the catalog corrected' and (0.5) '(b) counsel: require the assistant's pattern stopped, false claims retracted to misled buyers, discipline proportionate to an unrepented habit'. Total stays 5.0.

findings.detail: Line 4 bundles three checkable judgments: deliberateness+continuance named as Q151-h3 aggravating; still-ongoing/unrepented; buyers-harmed under Q145. All-or-nothing at 1.0 lets a grader lose the whole line over a partial answer.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the Q151-h3 deliberateness+continuance judgment as the scored core (it is one coherent head-claim); demote 'buyers harmed (Q145)' to non-scoring context in the key, OR make the line explicitly 'names Q151 head 3 deliberateness-and-continuance as aggravating' and drop the trailing conjuncts from the scoring text.

findings.quote: H3-continuance is also engaged (repeated, deliberate). But H3 is not the DISTINCT axis here
findings.detail: The key uses 'H3' for TWO different axes within one item: for (a) 'H3-continuance', for (b) 'H3 ... on the against-light/presumption axis'. The (a) head-pair enumeration reads '{(a) H2 ... by deliberate continuance}' while the (a) rubric line requires 'the repeated/continued withholding named'. A mid-tier grader gets ambiguous signal on whether (a)'s continuance is a scored h2 sub-element or an unscored h3 aside, and whether (b)'s 'H3' means the same head as (a)'s. Cross-item, other drafts use H3 to mean continuance; here (b)'s H3 means against-light. This risks inconsistent grading.
findings.proposed_fix: Relabel (b)'s axis explicitly (e.g. 'against-light/presumption (Q151 head 3, knowledge sub-head)') and keep (a) purely as 'H2 helplessness; year-long persistence is texture, not a second scored head' so 'H3' is not overloaded within the item and the accepted head-pair reads cleanly {(a) H2 helpless-dependent} vs {(b) against-light presumption}.

findings.detail: Three bundled judgments at 1.0: against-light presumption named; no-harm-as-grace-not-exculpation; single-episode-lighter note.

findings.quote: (b) profile: the act is the gravest KIND under Q113 (express blasphemous cursing of God) named as the aggravation
findings.detail: For (b) the scored 'head' is not a Q151-head at all but the KIND/quality of the act under Q113. The 0.5 gated head-pair line and (a)'s line are framed as Q151-heads (H1) but (b)'s scored aggravation is a Q113-kind claim, so 'incommensurable head-PAIR' pairs a Q151 head (H1) against a Q113 kind-of-sin. A mid-tier grader keying on 'name a Q151 head' per the pattern of the sibling contested items may mis-grade (b), since the accepted (b) element is 'gravest KIND ... express blasphemy', not a Q151 head number. This is graderable from the enumerated head-pair text, but the head-vs-kind asymmetry is a self-consistency wrinkle a mid-tier grader may trip on.
findings.proposed_fix: In the 0.5 gated line and (b) head line, add an explicit clause: 'for (b) the accepted incommensurable element is the gravest KIND-of-the-sin under Q113 (express blasphemy), NOT a Q151 head-number; naming that kind satisfies the criterion.' Keep as-is otherwise.
